# Two afternoons of data analysis

We will use R to explore biological data, inspect distributions, compare groups, and investigate correlations. You do not need previous R experience. The code is provided; your task is to understand the analysis and explain your decisions.

[Download the complete student project](statistics_lab_student.zip). Extract the ZIP, open `Statistics_lab.Rproj`, and keep the folder together. You can also browse the guides below before opening RStudio.

## Before the workshop

[Setup guide: Thursday's 30-minute installation session](notebooks/00_setup.html) · [R Markdown source](notebooks/00_setup.Rmd)

Watch the lecture assigned by the instructor. Bring your laptop to the installation session, or use a computer in the computer room.

## Day 1 — work through the examples together

| Notebook | What we will do | Editable source |
|---|---|---|
| [01. Importing data and basic statistics](notebooks/01_import_basics.html) | Run R commands, import MMSE and neurite tables, select values, and compare summaries | [Rmd](notebooks/01_import_basics.Rmd) |
| [02. Looking at the data](notebooks/02_visualisation.html) | Explore all three neurite conditions, vary histogram bins, compare boxplots and mean bars, and discuss a violin | [Rmd](notebooks/02_visualisation.Rmd) |
| [03. Normality, group comparisons and correlation](notebooks/03_statistical_analysis.html) | Inspect assumptions, compare Welch and Wilcoxon, and interpret a correlation | [Rmd](notebooks/03_statistical_analysis.Rmd) |

## Day 2 — your investigation

[04. Your MMSE investigation](notebooks/04_mmse_investigation.html) · [R Markdown source](notebooks/04_mmse_investigation.Rmd)

Work in pairs. Each student keeps a personal notebook containing code, figures, and their own explanations. Build a descriptive overview with summaries and plots, then complete one group comparison and one correlation, plus the short multiple-testing exercise. LLMs are available for hints, debugging, and explanations; you should understand the work you submit.

## References to keep beside you

- [Data dictionary and provenance](data/dictionary.html)
- [Short R command reference](notebooks/05_command_reference.html)
- The day 1 examples remain available during day 2.

Each afternoon lasts four hours, including breaks. Exercises labelled **Extra** are optional. Keep axis labels and interpretation; plot decoration can wait.
